concerns.text: The plan requires each of the ~50 selected repositories to contain **at least 5 LLM‑generated and 5 Human‑written blocks after tagging** (see "Target ≈ 50 active Python/JavaScript repos; minimum 5 LLM + 5 Human blocks per repo after filtering"). In practice, public repositories rarely expose LLM‑generated code via topics or keywords, and the classifier’s confidence filter (≥ 0.8) will further prune blocks. This makes the dataset requirement highly optimistic and likely unattainable, jeopardizing the matching step (FR‑008) and the validity of the downstream analysis.

The pipeline is slated to run on the **GitHub Actions free tier (2 CPU cores, ≈ 7 GB RAM, ≤ 6 h)** while processing up to 50 repositories, performing radon static analysis on all source files, ONNX CodeBERT inference on every extracted function/class, and propensity‑score matching. Even with shallow clones (depth = 100), the cumulative CPU time for classification (≈ 0.5 s per block) and radon analysis can easily exceed the 6‑hour wall‑clock limit, making the compute plan infeasible under the free‑tier constraints.
